title: Reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling, KV cache, batching
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: streaming token latency for short-turn chats was a dominant tail contributor for interactive applications. This PR implements a coordinated set of runtime improvements targeting the token emission path: 1) refactor token_loop to reduce blocking and minimize scheduling hops, 2) introduce an adaptive flush cadence FSM that flushes partial tokens earlier under interactive load patterns, 3) add a lightweight backpressure signal between batching/serving layers to avoid head-of-line stalls, 4) tweak kernel scheduler heuristics to prioritize low-latency streaming batches, 5) optimize KV cache read hot-paths for lock-free common-case reads, and 6) small continuous-batching adjustments to favor small low-latency batches for streaming routes. Changes are non-breaking to the public API and are backwards-compatible with existing routing and caching behavior. Benchmarks included below show median and p99 improvements on representative models. Rollout: staged canary with monitoring and fast rollback if latency regressions or error-rate increases are observed. Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests added, [x] integration latency tests added, [x] benchmark harness updated, [x] docs updated, [x] staged rollout plan prepared. Impact: reduces median token emission latency ~3-4x for short-turn chats while keeping throughput stable. See release_notes and benchmarks fields for numbers.
commits: Refactor token_loop to non-blocking flush and reduce scheduling hops
Add adaptive flush cadence finite-state machine with heuristic thresholds
Implement backpressure signal and handler between continuous_batcher and serving runtime
Adjust kernel_scheduler heuristics to prioritize streaming-critical batches
Optimize kv_cache read hot-path with lock-free fast path and metrics
Add end-to-end streaming latency integration tests and harness
benchmarks: median streaming token latency reduced from 85ms -> 22ms for short-turn chats (<=64 tokens)
end-to-end throughput stable (+3% under high concurrency due to reduced stalls)
microbench: token_loop non-blocking path reduces syscall/await overhead by ~60%
release_notes: Performance: reduce streaming token latency by ~3-4x for typical short-turn chats. No API changes. Rollout will be staged by model route and region. Monitoring: new streaming_latency per-route metric and alert on >20% regressions.
